note: The open-internet survey named detect-secrets (Yelp, Apache-2.0) as the clean, permissive tool to serve Nestor's 'never commit the trust root' refusal on top of the ruff+bandit it already runs. Wired into scripts/ci-lint.sh and the tests.yml lint job with a committed .secrets.baseline. The gate was shown to fail on a planted secret before being trusted.

decisions.question: How does the secret scan avoid tripping on the repo's own high-entropy test/derived data while still catching a real committed secret?
decisions.commitment: A committed .secrets.baseline records the only two current findings, both entropy hits on test fixtures with deliberately fake signatures (tests/test_seal_replacement.py, tests/test_sqlite_store.py); detect-secrets-hook fails only on findings NOT in the baseline. Derived and frequently-regenerated artifacts are EXCLUDED from the scan rather than baselined -- the binary store (docs/dogfood/nestor.db), the rebuilt decisions bundle (docs/dogfood/decisions.json), any exported *.bundle.json, and bench/results -- because their high-entropy content changes on every rebuild and would otherwise trip the hook on routine work. The same exclusion is applied in scripts/ci-lint.sh and .github/workflows/tests.yml.
decisions.why: A baseline that recorded the derived bundles would fail CI every time a decision was added (decisions.json regenerates with new content), turning a security gate into a nuisance that gets disabled. Excluding derived artifacts and baselining only stable source keeps the gate quiet on noise and loud on a genuinely new secret. The two baselined findings are fake signatures in test fixtures, not real secrets -- recorded as known rather than excluded because test source is exactly where a real secret could also hide, so it stays scanned.

decisions.question: Was the secret gate shown to actually fail, not just pass?
decisions.commitment: Yes. Before wiring it in, detect-secrets-hook was run against a planted file containing an AWS-shaped key and a high-entropy string; it exited non-zero and named both. Over the real tree (minus the excluded artifacts) it exits zero. A guard that cannot be shown to fail has not been shown to work.
decisions.why: The same rule the mutation guard (0083) enforces applies to this gate: a secret scanner that passes on everything, including a real secret, is a ledger, not a gate. Demonstrating the red before trusting the green is the acceptance test for the guard itself.
